scraped.scraped_description: A federated social network for individuals and communities to design, operate and control their own digital lives.

name: Bonfire
tagline: A federated social network for individuals and communities to design, operate and control their own digital lives.
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 - Peace Justice and Strong Institutions
known_funders: NGI (Next Generation Internet, EU-funded via NLnet)
dependency_risks: Competing with more established fediverse platforms (Mastodon)
outcome_methodology: Community feedback and adoption metrics; no formal evaluation framework
published_performance_metrics: GitHub activity metrics; Open Collective transparency reports; community engagement statistics
documented_limitations: Complex self-hosting compared to mainstream platforms
Smaller community than established fediverse alternatives
failure_modes: Low adoption velocity without network effects
curation_criteria: Community-driven moderation; extension-based approach allows communities to define their own content policies; AGPL-3.0 ensures code transparency and community control
contributor_governance: AGPL-3.0 licensed; open contributions via GitHub; modular extension system allows community-contributed extensions
disparity_tracking: Not formally tracked; project emphasizes accessibility and inclusion for marginalized communities through decentralized design
community_ownership: Finances transparently managed on Open Collective; community-driven development; no investor or VC involvement
ai_involvement: No AI/machine learning components; focus on human-centered, community-controlled design
political_relevance_summary: Addresses barriers to meaningful citizen participation in democratic decision-making by providing tools for public engagement and deliberation.

movement_building_utility.notes: Provides decentralized communication infrastructure as an alternative to corporate platforms.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase facilitates replication and adaptation. Already deployed across multiple jurisdictions (multiple countries), demonstrating cross-context adaptability.
